drugs.name: Ferrous sulfate (oral iron)
drugs.mechanism: Replaces depleted iron stores; absorbed as Fe2+ in the duodenum

drugs.name: Iron dextran / iron sucrose (IV iron)
drugs.disease: Iron deficiency anemia with malabsorption or rapid blood loss
drugs.mechanism: Parenteral iron repletion bypassing the closed gut

drugs.name: Deferoxamine
drugs.mechanism: Iron chelator that binds free iron for urinary excretion

drugs.name: Epoetin alfa (ESA)
drugs.disease: Anemia of chronic kidney disease or chemotherapy
drugs.mechanism: Binds EPO receptor on erythroid progenitors, activating JAK-STAT
drugs.adverseEffects: Thrombosis/stroke/MI if Hb pushed >11 g/dL (black box)

drugs.name: Hydroxyurea
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, inducing fetal hemoglobin (HbF)

drugs.name: Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit)
drugs.disease: Cyanide poisoning (also a form of B12)
drugs.mechanism: Binds cyanide to form non-toxic cyanocobalamin
drugs.adverseEffects: Reddish discoloration of skin and urine

drugs.name: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin)
drugs.mechanism: Cofactor for methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA conversion
drugs.adverseEffects: Well tolerated; must rule out before giving folate alone

drugs.name: Folic acid (folate)
drugs.mechanism: Restores tetrahydrofolate for DNA synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: Masks B12-deficiency anemia while neuropathy progresses (folate trap)

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.mechanism: Pro-drug; alkylates DNA at N7 of guanine causing cross-links
drugs.adverseEffects: Hemorrhagic cystitis from acrolein; prevented with MESNA

drugs.name: MESNA
drugs.mechanism: Thiol that concentrates in bladder and neutralizes acrolein

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.mechanism: Aquated intermediate cross-links DNA

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.mechanism: DNA cross-linking, less reactive than cisplatin

drugs.name: Oxaliplatin
drugs.mechanism: DNA cross-linking via aquated platinum intermediate

drugs.name: Methotrexate
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking active folate

drugs.name: Leucovorin (folinic acid)
drugs.mechanism: Reduced folate that bypasses blocked DHFR to rescue normal cells

drugs.name: 5-Fluorouracil
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits thymidylate synthase causing thymine-less death

drugs.name: Cytarabine (Ara-C)
drugs.mechanism: Arabinose analog blocks DNA polymerase and terminates chains

drugs.name: 6-Mercaptopurine
drugs.mechanism: Purine analog inactivated by xanthine oxidase
drugs.adverseEffects: Toxic accumulation with allopurinol; reduce dose 75%

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.mechanism: Blocks microtubule assembly, arresting mitosis
drugs.adverseEffects: Peripheral neuropathy, constipation; fatal if given intrathecally

drugs.name: Paclitaxel (taxane)
drugs.mechanism: Hyperstabilizes microtubules, blocking disassembly

drugs.name: Irinotecan
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits topoisomerase I, causing DNA strand breaks

drugs.name: Etoposide
drugs.mechanism: Blocks topoisomerase II resealing of double-strand DNA breaks

drugs.name: Doxorubicin (Red Devil)
drugs.mechanism: Generates free radicals and intercalates DNA

drugs.name: Bleomycin
drugs.mechanism: Generates free radicals causing DNA strand breaks

drugs.name: Carmustine / lomustine (nitrosoureas)
drugs.mechanism: Lipophilic alkylating agents that cross the blood-brain barrier

drugs.name: Imatinib
drugs.mechanism: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor blocking BCR-ABL ATP-binding site
drugs.adverseEffects: Periorbital edema; T315I mutation confers resistance

drugs.name: Erlotinib / gefitinib
drugs.mechanism: Small-molecule EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor

drugs.name: Trastuzumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against the HER2/neu receptor

drugs.name: Bevacizumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody that binds and neutralizes VEGF

drugs.name: Cetuximab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against EGFR
drugs.adverseEffects: Ineffective if KRAS is mutated; acneiform rash

drugs.name: Rituximab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody targeting CD20 on B cells

drugs.name: Bortezomib
drugs.mechanism: Proteasome inhibitor blocking NF-kB; misfolded proteins accumulate

drugs.name: Lenalidomide
drugs.mechanism: Binds cereblon, degrading transcription factors cancer cells need

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab
drugs.disease: Metastatic melanoma and other cancers (checkpoint inhibitor)
drugs.mechanism: PD-1 inhibitor that releases the brakes on T cells

drugs.name: Ipilimumab
drugs.mechanism: CTLA-4 inhibitor that enhances T-cell activation

drugs.name: CAR T-cell therapy
drugs.mechanism: Patient T cells engineered to recognize tumor antigen CD19
drugs.adverseEffects: Cytokine release syndrome (high fever, multi-organ failure)

drugs.name: ATRA (all-trans retinoic acid)
drugs.mechanism: Forces malignant promyelocytes to differentiate and mature

drugs.name: Eculizumab
drugs.mechanism: Anti-C5 monoclonal antibody blocking terminal complement
drugs.adverseEffects: Increased risk of Neisseria meningitidis infection

drugs.name: RhoGAM (anti-D immunoglobulin)
drugs.disease: Prevention of Rh hemolytic disease of the newborn
drugs.mechanism: Passive anti-D IgG clears fetal RBCs before maternal sensitization
drugs.adverseEffects: Well tolerated; given at 28 weeks and within 72h of delivery

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.mechanism: Antifibrinolytic that prevents clot dissolution

correlates.name: Bombay phenotype (Oh)
correlates.pathophysiology: Homozygous non-functional H gene means no H-substance, so no A or B antigens form and anti-H is produced
correlates.treatment: Can only receive blood from another Bombay donor

correlates.name: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN)
correlates.pathophysiology: Sensitized Rh-negative mother makes IgG anti-D that crosses the placenta to destroy fetal Rh+ RBCs
correlates.treatment: RhoGAM prophylaxis; in utero or exchange transfusion plus phototherapy

correlates.name: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (AHTR)
correlates.pathophysiology: ABO incompatibility (clerical error); preformed IgM fixes complement causing intravascular hemolysis
correlates.treatment: Stop transfusion; IV fluids, pressors, diuresis for renal protection

correlates.name: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO)
correlates.pathophysiology: Volume overload causes cardiogenic pulmonary edema with elevated CVP/PCWP
correlates.treatment: Diuretics (furosemide); slow infusion rate

correlates.name: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI)
correlates.pathophysiology: Donor anti-neutrophil antibodies activate recipient pulmonary neutrophils; non-cardiogenic edema with normal CVP
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; avoid implicated donors

correlates.name: Transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease (TA-GVHD)
correlates.pathophysiology: Donor T cells engraft in an immunocompromised host and attack host tissues
correlates.treatment: Prevented by irradiation of blood products; >90% fatal once established

correlates.name: Extramedullary hematopoiesis
correlates.pathophysiology: Failing bone marrow shifts blood cell production back to fetal sites, the liver and spleen
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause (e.g., myelofibrosis); supportive transfusion

correlates.name: Acute leukemia (marrow crowding)
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant blast expansion fills marrow, crowding out normal lineages causing pancytopenia
correlates.treatment: Induction chemotherapy; lineage-directed therapy after flow cytometry

correlates.name: Iron deficiency anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Iron loss or increased demand outpaces intake, depleting stores for hemoglobin synthesis
correlates.treatment: Oral ferrous sulfate; identify and treat the bleeding source

correlates.name: Anemia of chronic disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic inflammation (IL-6) raises hepcidin, locking iron in macrophages
correlates.treatment: Treat the underlying inflammatory disease

correlates.name: Sideroblastic anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Defective protoporphyrin synthesis causes iron to accumulate in mitochondria as ringed sideroblasts
correlates.treatment: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6); remove offending agent (alcohol, isoniazid)

correlates.name: Lead poisoning
correlates.pathophysiology: Lead inhibits ALAD and ferrochelatase, impairing heme synthesis; basophilic stippling appears
correlates.treatment: Chelation (e.g., succimer, EDTA, dimercaprol)

correlates.name: Alpha-thalassemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Deletion of alpha-globin genes on chromosome 16 reduces alpha-chain synthesis
correlates.treatment: Supportive; severe HbH disease may need transfusion; Hb Bart's is lethal

correlates.name: Beta-thalassemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Beta-globin gene mutations on chromosome 11 reduce beta-chain synthesis; elevated HbA2
correlates.treatment: Major: chronic transfusion with iron chelation; minor: none needed

correlates.name: Plummer-Vinson syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Iron deficiency anemia associated with esophageal webs and atrophic glossitis
correlates.treatment: Iron repletion; dilation of esophageal webs if needed

correlates.name: Megaloblastic anemia (B12/folate deficiency)
correlates.pathophysiology: Impaired DNA synthesis from B12 or folate deficiency causes large cells and hypersegmented neutrophils
correlates.treatment: Replace the deficient vitamin; confirm B12 status before giving folate

correlates.name: Subacute combined degeneration
correlates.pathophysiology: B12 deficiency raises methylmalonic acid, damaging dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts
correlates.treatment: B12 replacement; deficits may be irreversible if delayed

correlates.name: Hereditary spherocytosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Defects in ankyrin, spectrin, or band 3 cause membrane loss and rigid spheres trapped in the spleen
correlates.treatment: Splenectomy

correlates.name: Sickle cell disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Glutamate-to-valine mutation in beta-globin; HbS polymerizes under hypoxia/acidosis
correlates.treatment: Hydroxyurea; hydration, analgesia, vaccination against encapsulated organisms

correlates.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)
correlates.pathophysiology: Acquired PIGA mutation removes GPI-anchored CD55/CD59, leaving RBCs defenseless against complement
correlates.treatment: Eculizumab (anti-C5)

correlates.name: G6PD deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Lack of NADPH leaves RBCs vulnerable to oxidative stress, denaturing hemoglobin into Heinz bodies
correlates.treatment: Avoid oxidant triggers (fava beans, sulfa drugs); supportive care

correlates.name: Aplastic anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Marrow failure with fatty replacement causing pancytopenia
correlates.treatment: Immunosuppression or hematopoietic stem cell transplant

correlates.name: Fanconi anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Inherited defect in DNA cross-link repair causing pancytopenia
correlates.treatment: Hematopoietic stem cell transplant; supportive care

correlates.name: Diamond-Blackfan anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Congenital pure red cell aplasia with intrinsic ribosomal defect
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids; transfusion support

correlates.name: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
correlates.pathophysiology: Clonal expansion of myeloid blasts; Auer rods of crystallized myeloperoxidase
correlates.treatment: Induction chemotherapy (e.g., cytarabine-based)

correlates.name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL/M3)
correlates.pathophysiology: t(15;17) disrupts the retinoic acid receptor; granule release triggers DIC
correlates.treatment: ATRA (all-trans retinoic acid) to force differentiation

correlates.name: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Clonal proliferation of TdT-positive lymphoblasts; most common childhood cancer
correlates.treatment: Multi-agent chemotherapy with CNS prophylaxis

correlates.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Accumulation of fragile mature B cells; smudge cells and hypogammaglobulinemia
correlates.treatment: BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib); watch-and-wait if asymptomatic

correlates.name: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML)
correlates.pathophysiology: Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) creates the constitutively active BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase
correlates.treatment: Imatinib or other BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors

correlates.name: Follicular lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: t(14;18) overexpresses anti-apoptotic BCL-2, so cells refuse to die
correlates.treatment: Watch-and-wait; rituximab-based therapy when symptomatic

correlates.name: Burkitt lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: t(8;14) overexpresses c-MYC; fastest-growing tumor with starry-sky histology
correlates.treatment: Intensive chemotherapy with tumor lysis prophylaxis (hydration, rasburicase)

correlates.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+/CD30+) secrete cytokines summoning a reactive infiltrate; contiguous nodal spread
correlates.treatment: ABVD chemotherapy

correlates.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Most common adult NHL; rapidly enlarging mass, often extranodal, may arise de novo or from transformation
correlates.treatment: R-CHOP; CAR-T for relapsed disease

correlates.name: Mantle cell lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: t(11;14) overexpresses cyclin D1, pushing cells past the G1/S checkpoint; CD5+/CD23-
correlates.treatment: Chemoimmunotherapy; BTK inhibitors

correlates.name: MALT lymphoma (marginal zone)
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic mucosal inflammation (H. pylori, Sjogren, Hashimoto) drives clonal B-cell proliferation
correlates.treatment: H. pylori eradication can cure gastric MALT lymphoma

correlates.name: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL)
correlates.pathophysiology: HTLV-1 retrovirus drives malignant T cells; flower cells, lytic bone lesions, hypercalcemia
correlates.treatment: Combination chemotherapy; antiviral plus interferon regimens

correlates.name: Mycosis fungoides
correlates.pathophysiology: Indolent skin-homing CD4+ T-cell lymphoma with Pautrier microabscesses
correlates.treatment: Skin-directed therapy (topical steroids, phototherapy)

correlates.name: Multiple myeloma
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant plasma cell clone produces an M-spike causing CRAB (hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia, lytic bone lesions)
correlates.treatment: Lenalidomide + bortezomib + dexamethasone (RVd)

correlates.name: MGUS
correlates.pathophysiology: M-protein <3 g/dL with <10% marrow plasma cells and no end-organ damage
correlates.treatment: Lifelong surveillance; progresses to myeloma ~1% per year

correlates.name: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma producing IgM (MYD88 L265P); no lytic bone lesions
correlates.treatment: Plasmapheresis for hyperviscosity; BTK inhibitors

correlates.name: AL amyloidosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Misfolded light chains deposit as beta-pleated sheets in tissues; macroglossia, restrictive cardiomyopathy
correlates.treatment: Plasma-cell-directed chemotherapy; Congo red confirms diagnosis

correlates.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Massive tumor cell death releases uric acid, potassium, and phosphate causing metabolic derangement
correlates.treatment: Aggressive hydration plus allopurinol or rasburicase

correlates.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
correlates.pathophysiology: Widespread activation of coagulation consumes clotting factors and platelets
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause; FFP, cryoprecipitate, and platelet support
